subject: Request: temporary latency guarantee for Quantix demo week
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@quantix.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Mallory <chris.mallory@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request for temporary latency guarantee during demo week

Hi Jonas,

Hope you’re well — Quantix is scheduled to run a set of customer-facing demos the week of Dec 13–17. Based on our runbook we need an explicit latency target for the demo environment (p95 <= 180ms) for that window to avoid timeouts in the orchestration layer. Our success metric for the week is demo completion rate > 95%.

We know this is outside the standard hosted API commitments, but given this is a time-bound event tied to our renewal conversation, can Redwood confirm a temporary, narrowly scoped latency guarantee (Dec 13 00:00 UTC through Dec 18 00:00 UTC)? We can sign a short side-letter or accept a financial holdback if needed — attaching our demo load estimates.

Attachments: demo-load-estimates-dec2026.xlsx

Thank you — Elena

--
Elena Soto
Director of Product Ops, Quantix Analytics
elena@quantix.ai
+1 415-555-0124
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@quantix.ai>
Cc: Chris Mallory <chris.mallory@quantix.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request for temporary latency guarantee during demo week

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the load sheet. Looping in Dev (infra) and Laura (legal/finance) to scope risk and the approvals path. A few quick questions from my side:

- Is the traffic origin regionally concentrated (us-west), or will it come globally?
- Is Quantix okay with a scoped window and an agreed fallback (e.g., Redwood routes to a slightly higher-latency variant if load exceeds projections)?

We’ll respond formally by EOD tomorrow after a quick infra feasibility check.

Best,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@quantix.ai>, Chris Mallory <chris.mallory@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request for temporary latency guarantee during demo week

On Thu, Dec 2, 2026 at 11:02 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the load sheet. Looping in Dev (infra) and Laura (legal/finance) to scope risk and the approvals path. A few quick questions from my side:
>
> - Is the traffic origin regionally concentrated (us-west), or will it come globally?
> - Is Quantix okay with a scoped window and an agreed fallback (e.g., Redwood routes to a slightly higher-latency variant if load exceeds projections)?

Thanks — I ran the numbers against our capacity models and the attached traffic CSV. Short answer: technically feasible with short-term reserved capacity (we can reserve a dedicated pool for the week) plus tighter batching controls and KV prefix caching for demo prefixes. Estimated incremental cost: ~1.6x run-rate for that window.

Risks/notes:
- If traffic spikes 2x beyond the XLS, we will see p95 erosion; fallback to a larger-quantized model will increase latency to ~350ms.
- We’ll need a confirmed cutover play (who triggers reserve capacity) and a single on-call owner from Quantix during the window.
- Provisioning lead time: 48–72 hours to spin reserved nodes and validate perf tests.

I attached the parsed traffic summary and a first-draft SLA snippet for review.

Attachments: quantix_traffic_report_nov2026.csv, proposed-sla-draft-quantix-v1.pdf

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-12-04T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request for temporary latency guarantee during demo week

Jonas / Dev —

Thanks for the assessment. A few commercial / compliance points to flag:

- We can approve a time-boxed addendum that defines a temporary SLA (p95 <= 180ms) from Dec 13 00:00 UTC — Dec 18 00:00 UTC, but it must include: a) explicit traffic threshold that Quantix commits not to exceed, b) a financial holdback clause for degradation beyond threshold, and c) a rollback/fallback clause (we will fail over to the standard tier if safeguards trigger).
- Finance needs the estimated incremental charge (Dev’s 1.6x figure) broken down into a dollar amount and invoicing cadence.
- Legal requests that we limit indemnities and include a short force-majeure carve-out for network-level outages.

If Quantix agrees to the above, I can route a concise addendum to sign-off quickly. Recommend naming Hannah Schmitt for executive approval if the dollar uplift exceeds $50k.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@quantix.ai>
Date: 2026-12-06T17:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request for temporary latency guarantee during demo week

Thanks everyone for the quick triage and the clear options laid out. I approve a narrow, time-boxed SLA addendum under the commercial guardrails Laura outlined. Conditions:

1) Quantix signs the addendum confirming the traffic threshold and the financial holdback.
2) Dev to own provisioning runbook and a production smoke test 24 hours before the window.
3) Jonas to secure a signed addendum by Dec 10 COB.
4) Finance to issue a temporary invoice for the uplift; if uplift > $50k, I will require a brief exec note but will not block.

Jonas — please route the addendum (use the attached draft) and confirm when Quantix has signed.

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
